key_insight: MCL-PINNs combines phase-field physics with a discrete-time, multi-network PINN design to better capture sharp interfaces and moving contact lines with dynamic boundary conditions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a mesh-free solver option for interfacial flow problems in wetting, coating, and microfluidic systems where contact angle evolution and long-time stability matter.
method: Discrete-time time-marching with separate networks for successive steps
Relaxed output distribution constraint plus variable scaling for sharp phase-field profiles
Adaptive loss weighting and interface-focused collocation sampling; symmetry inputs when applicable
evidence_signal: The method was tested on three numerical examples—droplet coalescence, shear-induced deformation, and dynamic wetting in a heterogeneous channel—and reported improved accuracy and robustness over standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful tuning of adaptive weights, sampling, and scaling, and the approach may still be sensitive when interfaces become extremely sharp or long-time error accumulates.
paper_title: A phase-field neural solver for moving contact line problems with dynamic boundary conditions
